title: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication
description: Authentication middleware and handlers for ASP.NET Core applications.

data.text: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication provides the authentication infrastructure for ASP.NET Core. It supports cookies, JWT Bearer, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, and custom authentication schemes.

data.title: JWT Authentication

terms.definition: A named strategy for authenticating requests.
A token-based authentication scheme using JSON Web Tokens.

data.title: Security
data.text: Always validate tokens server-side and never expose signing keys to clients.

A scheme names a way to authenticate; a handler implements it. Cookie authentication stores a ticket in a cookie and validates it on each request, while JWT bearer validates a signed token presented in the `Authorization` header. When a request is unauthenticated, the handler challenge runs — a redirect to login for cookies, a 401 for JWT.

data.title: JWT bearer plus a policy
Authentication is not authorization
data.text: Authentication answers who the caller is; authorization answers what they may do. A token that validates is authenticated, but nothing about it grants access to a resource. The signing key must never leave the server, the audience and issuer must be validated to prevent a token from another service being accepted, and the authorization policy is the separate check that enforces access.

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: Use ASP.NET Core Authentication to secure your applications with industry-standard protocols.
